projects.name: django

excluded_paths_with_rationale.exclusion_rationale: ORM query compiler — irreducible algorithmic complexity per ADR-0.0.27 anti-pattern; would pull metric distributions toward leniency if measured.
Third-party-style contrib apps; not core framework design surface.
Backend adapters mirror upstream DB driver shapes; coupling profile is upstream-driven, not Django craft.

projects.path_filter_rationale: Measure forms / templates / generic views / utils / middleware — the stable framework-design surfaces that have aged across 5.x. Exclude ORM compiler (algorithmic complexity), contrib (separate quality bar), DB backends (upstream-shaped).
projects.longevity_evidence: Active development since 2005 (first public release 2005-07-21); 20+ years of continuous Python evolution.
projects.maintenance_health_evidence: Latest release 5.2.5 on 2025-08-06; 5.x series ships LTS and feature releases on a bounded cadence; security updates current.
projects.practitioner_reputation_citation: Cited in *Two Scoops of Django* (Greenfeld & Roy); PEP 3333 (WSGI) discussion; foundational reference for Python web framework design.
projects.craftsmanship_signal_narrative: Maintainer cohort includes Russell Keith-Magee, Carlton Gibson, and Jacob Kaplan-Moss — all PyCon-talk regulars and project-governance authors; team-shaped review discipline rather than dictator pattern; LTS release cadence demonstrates calibrated stability/innovation balance.
projects.project_doctrine_fitness_narrative: Pure-Python web framework, no Rust/C extensions in measured paths, ORM is opt-in (not coupled to non-DB usage), respects stdlib idioms in utils. Does not violate Stdlib-First (gzkit does not depend on Django; corpus is learning relationship, not adoption).

projects.path_filter_rationale: Measure the four PEP-anchored stdlib modules (pathlib / dataclasses / functools / contextlib) that exemplify Python stdlib-style design discipline — each is the reference for its idiom and each ships PEP-grounded API decisions. One corpus entry, four files, single craftsmanship narrative.
projects.longevity_evidence: CPython itself is the language; selected modules (functools, contextlib) date back 15+ years; pathlib (PEP 428, 2014); dataclasses (PEP 557, 2017).
projects.maintenance_health_evidence: Latest CPython release v3.15.0a8 on 2026-04-07; alpha series active; release cycle is the ecosystem's heartbeat.
projects.practitioner_reputation_citation: PEP 343 (contextlib), PEP 428 (pathlib), PEP 557 (dataclasses); core-developer authorship across these modules.
projects.craftsmanship_signal_narrative: Each selected module is the reference for its idiom — pathlib is the Path-object canon; dataclasses is the class-builder canon; functools.partial / lru_cache / singledispatch are higher-order-function canon; contextlib is the resource-management canon. PEP-driven authorship discipline.
projects.project_doctrine_fitness_narrative: Stdlib itself — the canonical reference for Stdlib-First. Pure-Python by definition for these modules. The most foundational craft signal in the corpus.
